newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended firmer on Wednesday, supported for most of the session by overnight gains on Wall Street, a stronger dollar and several pieces of corporate news.
The AEX index of Dutch main stocks closed 4.05 higher at 652.34, just below Monday's record close of 652.84, after peaking at 654.03 points.

Dealers said volatile early trade in New York undermined the Dutch market during its last hour. But they said the AEX would likely continue to edge up steadily, even after the release of key U.S. economic data at the end of the week.

"Institutional players usually have a lot of money to spend at the beginning of the year, which brings volume back into the market and pushes prices up," one dealer said, adding the economic climate was favourable for the Dutch share market.

"The probable outcome of the U.S. data is already discounted in the prices. Market players seem optimistic -- with some starting to buy back the calls (call options they wrote earlier) ahead of the options expiry," one dealer said, foreseeing an AEX level of 666 somewhere next week.
Philips starred, ending 2.50 guilders higher at 71.90 after a day of active trading.
Dealers said the stock rose both on technical factors and fundamentals. Some added it could rise towards 74-75 guilders.
Philips was boosted by news it was further loosening ties with ailing German unit Grundig and a broker upgrade.
Dealers said a surge in the share price of sector rival Nokia, interesting possibilities in the television decoder business and an outperforming semiconductor sector also underpinned the stock.
"There's also an essential technical point. After hovering below 70 guilders for quite some time, the shares have finally crossed the 70.50 guilders barrier," a dealer said.
"They now look set for a further rise to the next resistance level," he added.
Several midcap stocks also showed big gains, with some of them unusually active.
Transport and trading company Internatio-Mueller NV was among the ten most heavily traded stocks, with around five times the daily average changing hands.
Dealers were at a loss to explain the surge in volume. The stock added 1.60 to 46.60 guilders.
Pharmaceuticals wholesaler and producer OPG also ended up, gaining 2.30 guilders to 52.80 guilders.

Several retail stocks ended higher, benefiting from the acceleration in turnover growth in the Netherlands during the fourth quarter of 1996, as reflected in Ahold's 1996 sales figures published yesterday.
Supermarkets group De Boer Winkelbedrijven, which reported a 25 percent rise in 1996 turnover yesterday, added 2.80 guilders to end at 138.50, while Ahold added 1.50 guilders to 107.40.
